DINOv2 Comprehensive Embedding Evaluation — Before Fine-Tuning¶

This notebook performs a rigorous evaluation of frozen pretrained DINOv2 embeddings for the wheat-grain dataset.

Experiment plan¶

  1. Normalization + Feature Redundancy

    • Original
    • Gray-World (p=1)
    • Shades-of-Gray (p=4, p=6, p=8)
    • Max-RGB
    • CLS, mean patch-token, and CLS + mean-patch embeddings
    • PCA redundancy, effective rank, correlation, class structure

  2. Robustness

    • Blur
    • Gaussian noise
    • Brightness
    • Contrast
    • Warm/cool illumination cast
    • Resolution degradation

  3. DINOv2 Size Comparison

    • ViT-S/14
    • ViT-B/14

  4. Final evidence

    • Class separability
    • Source-image-excluded nearest-neighbor consistency
    • Feature redundancy
    • Robustness
    • Runtime / GPU memory
    • Model-size trade-off

Experimental rules¶

  • No DINOv2 fine-tuning.
  • No downstream classifier training.
  • Same representative subset in every experiment.
  • Balanced sampling by class with source-image diversity.
  • Same-source grains are excluded from KNN evaluation.
  • Color constancy is estimated using grain pixels only.
  • Aspect ratio is preserved before DINOv2 resize.
  • Embeddings are cached so the experiment can resume safely.

IMAGE_EXTENSIONS = {".jpg", ".jpeg", ".png", ".bmp", ".tif", ".tiff", ".webp"}

def read_class_names(dataset_dir: Path):
    yaml_candidates = list(dataset_dir.glob("*.yaml")) + list(dataset_dir.glob("*.yml"))

    for yaml_path in yaml_candidates:
        try:
            cfg = yaml.safe_load(yaml_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            names = cfg.get("names")

            if isinstance(names, list):
                return {i: str(name) for i, name in enumerate(names)}, yaml_path

            if isinstance(names, dict):
                return {int(k): str(v) for k, v in names.items()}, yaml_path

        except Exception:
            pass

    return {}, None


def find_split_pairs(dataset_dir: Path):
    aliases = [("train", "train"), ("valid", "valid"), ("val", "val"), ("test", "test")]
    found = []

    for split_name, folder in aliases:
        image_dir = dataset_dir / folder / "images"
        label_dir = dataset_dir / folder / "labels"

        if image_dir.exists() and label_dir.exists():
            found.append((split_name, image_dir, label_dir))

    for split_name, folder in aliases:
        image_dir = dataset_dir / "images" / folder
        label_dir = dataset_dir / "labels" / folder

        candidate = (split_name, image_dir, label_dir)

        if image_dir.exists() and label_dir.exists() and candidate not in found:
            found.append(candidate)

    return found

5. Parse YOLO segmentation labels¶

In [5]:
def parse_yolo_segmentation_line(line: str):
    parts = line.strip().split()

    if len(parts) < 7:
        return None

    class_id = int(float(parts[0]))
    coords = np.asarray([float(v) for v in parts[1:]], dtype=np.float32)

    if coords.size % 2 != 0:
        return None

    polygon_norm = coords.reshape(-1, 2)

    if polygon_norm.shape[0] < 3:
        return None

    return class_id, polygon_norm


records = []

for split_name, image_dir, label_dir in SPLIT_DIRS:
    image_paths = [
        path
        for path in image_dir.rglob("*")
        if path.suffix.lower() in IMAGE_EXTENSIONS
    ]

    for image_path in tqdm(image_paths, desc=f"Parse {split_name}"):
        label_path = label_dir / f"{image_path.stem}.txt"

        if not label_path.exists():
            relative_label = image_path.relative_to(image_dir).with_suffix(".txt")
            label_path = label_dir / relative_label

        if not label_path.exists():
            continue

        try:
            with Image.open(image_path) as image:
                width, height = image.size
        except Exception:
            continue

        lines = label_path.read_text(
            encoding="utf-8",
            errors="ignore",
        ).splitlines()

        for instance_idx, line in enumerate(lines):
            parsed = parse_yolo_segmentation_line(line)

            if parsed is None:
                continue

            class_id, polygon_norm = parsed

            polygon_px = polygon_norm.copy()
            polygon_px[:, 0] *= width
            polygon_px[:, 1] *= height

            records.append({
                "split": split_name,
                "image_path": str(image_path),
                "label_path": str(label_path),
                "instance_idx": int(instance_idx),
                "class_id": int(class_id),
                "class_name": CLASS_NAMES.get(class_id, f"class_{class_id}"),
                "polygon_px": polygon_px,
                "image_width": int(width),
                "image_height": int(height),
            })

instances_df = pd.DataFrame(records)

6. Balanced source-diverse representative subset¶

In [6]:
def diverse_balanced_sample(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    target_per_class: int,
    seed: int = 42,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    # The within-source rank makes the sampler prefer broad source-image
    # coverage before selecting many grains from one image.
    pieces = []

    for class_id, class_df in df.groupby("class_id"):
        class_df = class_df.sample(
            frac=1.0,
            random_state=seed + int(class_id),
        ).copy()

        class_df["_within_source_rank"] = (
            class_df.groupby("image_path").cumcount()
        )

        class_df = class_df.sort_values(
            ["_within_source_rank", "image_path", "instance_idx"]
        )

        n_take = min(target_per_class, len(class_df))

        selected = class_df.iloc[:n_take].drop(
            columns="_within_source_rank"
        )

        pieces.append(selected)

    subset = pd.concat(pieces, ignore_index=True)

    subset = subset.sample(
        frac=1.0,
        random_state=seed,
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    subset["row_id"] = np.arange(len(subset), dtype=np.int64)

    return subset

    target_per_class=TARGET_PER_CLASS,
    seed=SEED,
)

7. Crop, mask, normalization, and perturbation functions¶

In [8]:
@lru_cache(maxsize=64)
def _read_rgb_cached(image_path: str) -> np.ndarray:
    bgr = cv2.imread(image_path, cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)

    if bgr is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not read image: {image_path}")

    return cv2.cvtColor(bgr, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)


def extract_crop_and_mask(
    image_path: str,
    polygon_px: np.ndarray,
    padding_ratio: float = 0.08,
) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    image_rgb = _read_rgb_cached(str(image_path))
    h, w = image_rgb.shape[:2]

    polygon = np.round(
        np.asarray(polygon_px)
    ).astype(np.int32)

    x, y, bw, bh = cv2.boundingRect(polygon)

    pad_x = int(round(bw * padding_ratio))
    pad_y = int(round(bh * padding_ratio))

    x1 = max(0, x - pad_x)
    y1 = max(0, y - pad_y)
    x2 = min(w, x + bw + pad_x)
    y2 = min(h, y + bh + pad_y)

    crop = image_rgb[y1:y2, x1:x2].copy()

    local_polygon = polygon.copy()
    local_polygon[:, 0] -= x1
    local_polygon[:, 1] -= y1

    mask = np.zeros(crop.shape[:2], dtype=np.uint8)
    cv2.fillPoly(mask, [local_polygon], 255)

    return crop, mask


def apply_mask_background(
    image_rgb: np.ndarray,
    mask: np.ndarray,
    background_value: int = 127,
) -> np.ndarray:
    background = np.full_like(
        image_rgb,
        int(background_value),
    )

    return np.where(
        mask[..., None] > 0,
        image_rgb,
        background,
    ).astype(np.uint8)


def _valid_color_pixels(
    image_rgb: np.ndarray,
    mask: Optional[np.ndarray],
) -> np.ndarray:
    pixels = (
        image_rgb[mask > 0]
        if mask is not None
        else image_rgb.reshape(-1, 3)
    )

    if pixels.size == 0:
        return pixels.astype(np.float32)

    pixels = pixels.astype(np.float32)

    intensity = pixels.mean(axis=1)

    valid = (
        (intensity >= COLOR_CONSTANCY_MIN_INTENSITY)
        & (intensity <= COLOR_CONSTANCY_MAX_INTENSITY)
    )

    if valid.sum() >= 10:
        pixels = pixels[valid]

    return pixels


def shades_of_gray_color_constancy(
    image_rgb: np.ndarray,
    mask: Optional[np.ndarray],
    p: float = 6.0,
    eps: float = 1e-6,
) -> np.ndarray:
    pixels = _valid_color_pixels(image_rgb, mask)

    if pixels.size == 0:
        return image_rgb.copy()

    pixels_01 = np.clip(
        pixels / 255.0,
        0.0,
        1.0,
    )

    illuminant = (
        np.mean(
            np.power(pixels_01, p),
            axis=0,
        )
        + eps
    ) ** (1.0 / p)

    target = float(np.mean(illuminant))

    gains = target / np.maximum(
        illuminant,
        eps,
    )

    corrected = (
        image_rgb.astype(np.float32)
        * gains.reshape(1, 1, 3)
    )

    return np.clip(
        corrected,
        0,
        255,
    ).astype(np.uint8)


def max_rgb_color_constancy(
    image_rgb: np.ndarray,
    mask: Optional[np.ndarray],
    eps: float = 1e-6,
) -> np.ndarray:
    pixels = _valid_color_pixels(image_rgb, mask)

    if pixels.size == 0:
        return image_rgb.copy()

    illuminant = np.maximum(
        pixels.max(axis=0),
        eps,
    )

    target = float(np.mean(illuminant))
    gains = target / illuminant

    corrected = (
        image_rgb.astype(np.float32)
        * gains.reshape(1, 1, 3)
    )

    return np.clip(
        corrected,
        0,
        255,
    ).astype(np.uint8)


def apply_normalization(
    image_rgb: np.ndarray,
    mask: np.ndarray,
    spec: dict,
) -> np.ndarray:
    kind = spec["kind"]

    if kind == "none":
        return image_rgb.copy()

    if kind == "shades_of_gray":
        return shades_of_gray_color_constancy(
            image_rgb,
            mask,
            p=float(spec["p"]),
        )

    if kind == "max_rgb":
        return max_rgb_color_constancy(
            image_rgb,
            mask,
        )

    raise ValueError(f"Unknown normalization kind: {kind}")


def apply_perturbation(
    image_rgb: np.ndarray,
    spec: dict,
    seed: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    kind = spec["kind"]

    if kind == "none":
        return image_rgb.copy()

    image_f = image_rgb.astype(np.float32)

    if kind == "gaussian_blur":
        sigma = float(spec["sigma"])

        output = cv2.GaussianBlur(
            image_rgb,
            (0, 0),
            sigmaX=sigma,
            sigmaY=sigma,
        )

        return output.astype(np.uint8)

    if kind == "gaussian_noise":
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

        noise = rng.normal(
            0.0,
            float(spec["std"]),
            size=image_f.shape,
        ).astype(np.float32)

        return np.clip(
            image_f + noise,
            0,
            255,
        ).astype(np.uint8)

    if kind == "brightness":
        factor = float(spec["factor"])

        return np.clip(
            image_f * factor,
            0,
            255,
        ).astype(np.uint8)

    if kind == "contrast":
        factor = float(spec["factor"])

        mean = image_f.mean(
            axis=(0, 1),
            keepdims=True,
        )

        output = (
            (image_f - mean) * factor
            + mean
        )

        return np.clip(
            output,
            0,
            255,
        ).astype(np.uint8)

    if kind == "channel_gain":
        gains = np.asarray(
            spec["gains"],
            dtype=np.float32,
        ).reshape(1, 1, 3)

        return np.clip(
            image_f * gains,
            0,
            255,
        ).astype(np.uint8)

    if kind == "resolution":
        scale = float(spec["scale"])

        h, w = image_rgb.shape[:2]

        low_w = max(1, int(round(w * scale)))
        low_h = max(1, int(round(h * scale)))

        low = cv2.resize(
            image_rgb,
            (low_w, low_h),
            interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA,
        )

        restored = cv2.resize(
            low,
            (w, h),
            interpolation=cv2.INTER_CUBIC,
        )

        return restored.astype(np.uint8)

    raise ValueError(f"Unknown perturbation kind: {kind}")

8. DINOv2 preprocessing with aspect-ratio preservation¶

In [9]:
DINO_NORMALIZE = transforms.Normalize(
    mean=(0.485, 0.456, 0.406),
    std=(0.229, 0.224, 0.225),
)

TO_TENSOR = transforms.ToTensor()


def pad_to_square(
    image: Image.Image,
    fill_value: int = 127,
) -> Image.Image:
    width, height = image.size
    side = max(width, height)

    canvas = Image.new(
        "RGB",
        (side, side),
        color=(fill_value, fill_value, fill_value),
    )

    left = (side - width) // 2
    top = (side - height) // 2

    canvas.paste(
        image,
        (left, top),
    )

    return canvas


def prepare_dino_tensor(
    image_rgb: np.ndarray,
    resize_mode: str = "aspect_pad",
) -> torch.Tensor:
    image = Image.fromarray(image_rgb)

    if resize_mode == "aspect_pad":
        image = pad_to_square(
            image,
            fill_value=MASK_BACKGROUND,
        )

    elif resize_mode != "stretch":
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown resize mode: {resize_mode}"
        )

    image = image.resize(
        (IMAGE_SIZE, IMAGE_SIZE),
        resample=Image.Resampling.BICUBIC,
    )

    tensor = TO_TENSOR(image)
    tensor = DINO_NORMALIZE(tensor)

    return tensor

def get_normalization_spec(name: str):
    for spec in NORMALIZATION_SPECS:
        if spec["name"] == name:
            return spec

    raise KeyError(name)


preview_rows = subset_df.sample(
    n=min(6, len(subset_df)),
    random_state=SEED,
)

for _, row in preview_rows.iterrows():
    crop, mask = extract_crop_and_mask(
        row["image_path"],
        row["polygon_px"],
        PADDING_RATIO,
    )

    original = apply_mask_background(
        crop,
        mask,
        MASK_BACKGROUND,
    )

    corrected = apply_normalization(
        crop,
        mask,
        get_normalization_spec("shades_gray_p6"),
    )

    corrected = apply_mask_background(
        corrected,
        mask,
        MASK_BACKGROUND,
    )

    plt.figure(figsize=(4, 4))
    plt.imshow(original)
    plt.title(f"Original — {row['class_name']}")
    plt.axis("off")
    plt.show()

    plt.figure(figsize=(4, 4))
    plt.imshow(corrected)
    plt.title(f"Shades-of-Gray p=6 — {row['class_name']}")
    plt.axis("off")
    plt.show()

class GrainConditionDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(
        self,
        dataframe: pd.DataFrame,
        normalization_spec: dict,
        perturbation_spec: dict,
        resize_mode: str,
    ):
        self.df = dataframe.reset_index(drop=True)
        self.normalization_spec = normalization_spec
        self.perturbation_spec = perturbation_spec
        self.resize_mode = resize_mode

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.df)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        row = self.df.iloc[idx]

        crop, mask = extract_crop_and_mask(
            row["image_path"],
            row["polygon_px"],
            PADDING_RATIO,
        )

        # Realistic order:
        # acquisition degradation -> color constancy -> mask -> DINO preprocessing.
        perturbed = apply_perturbation(
            crop,
            self.perturbation_spec,
            seed=SEED + int(row["row_id"]),
        )

        normalized = apply_normalization(
            perturbed,
            mask,
            self.normalization_spec,
        )

        masked = apply_mask_background(
            normalized,
            mask,
            MASK_BACKGROUND,
        )

        tensor = prepare_dino_tensor(
            masked,
            self.resize_mode,
        )

        return tensor, int(row["row_id"])

11. DINOv2 model loading and safe cached extraction¶

In [13]:
def load_dino_model(model_key: str):
    config = MODEL_CONFIGS[model_key]

    try:
        model = torch.hub.load(
            "facebookresearch/dinov2",
            config["hub_name"],
            pretrained=True,
            trust_repo=True,
        )
    except TypeError:
        model = torch.hub.load(
            "facebookresearch/dinov2",
            config["hub_name"],
            pretrained=True,
        )

    model = model.to(DEVICE)
    model.eval()

    for parameter in model.parameters():
        parameter.requires_grad = False

    num_params = sum(
        parameter.numel()
        for parameter in model.parameters()
    )

    return model, num_params


def release_model(model):
    del model
    gc.collect()

    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()


def condition_cache_path(
    model_key: str,
    normalization_name: str,
    perturbation_name: str,
):
    filename = (
        f"{model_key}"
        f"__{normalization_name}"
        f"__{perturbation_name}"
        f"__{RESIZE_MODE}.npz"
    )

    return CACHE_DIR / filename


def _extract_once(
    model,
    model_key: str,
    normalization_spec: dict,
    perturbation_spec: dict,
    batch_size: int,
):
    dataset = GrainConditionDataset(
        subset_df,
        normalization_spec,
        perturbation_spec,
        RESIZE_MODE,
    )

    loader = DataLoader(
        dataset,
        batch_size=batch_size,
        shuffle=False,
        num_workers=0,
        pin_memory=(DEVICE == "cuda"),
    )

    cls_parts = []
    patch_parts = []
    row_id_parts = []

    if DEVICE == "cuda":
        torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()

    started = time.perf_counter()

    with torch.inference_mode():
        for images, row_ids in tqdm(
            loader,
            desc=(
                f"{model_key} | "
                f"{normalization_spec['name']} | "
                f"{perturbation_spec['name']} | "
                f"bs={batch_size}"
            ),
        ):
            images = images.to(
                DEVICE,
                non_blocking=True,
            )

            if DEVICE == "cuda":
                with torch.autocast(
                    device_type="cuda",
                    dtype=torch.float16,
                ):
                    features = model.forward_features(images)

                    cls_embedding = features["x_norm_clstoken"]

                    mean_patch = (
                        features["x_norm_patchtokens"]
                        .mean(dim=1)
                    )
            else:
                features = model.forward_features(images)

                cls_embedding = features["x_norm_clstoken"]

                mean_patch = (
                    features["x_norm_patchtokens"]
                    .mean(dim=1)
                )

            cls_parts.append(
                cls_embedding.float().cpu().numpy()
            )

            patch_parts.append(
                mean_patch.float().cpu().numpy()
            )

            row_id_parts.append(
                row_ids.numpy()
            )

    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started

    cls_array = np.concatenate(
        cls_parts,
        axis=0,
    )

    patch_array = np.concatenate(
        patch_parts,
        axis=0,
    )

    row_ids = np.concatenate(
        row_id_parts,
        axis=0,
    )

    concat_array = np.concatenate(
        [cls_array, patch_array],
        axis=1,
    )

    if DEVICE == "cuda":
        peak_gpu_mb = (
            torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()
            / (1024 ** 2)
        )
    else:
        peak_gpu_mb = np.nan

    return {
        "row_ids": row_ids,
        "cls": cls_array,
        "mean_patch": patch_array,
        "cls_mean_concat": concat_array,
        "elapsed_sec": float(elapsed),
        "grains_per_sec": float(
            len(row_ids) / max(elapsed, 1e-9)
        ),
        "peak_gpu_mb": float(peak_gpu_mb),
        "batch_size": int(batch_size),
    }


def extract_embeddings(
    model,
    model_key: str,
    normalization_spec: dict,
    perturbation_spec: dict,
    initial_batch_size: int,
):
    cache_path = condition_cache_path(
        model_key,
        normalization_spec["name"],
        perturbation_spec["name"],
    )

    expected_row_ids = (
        subset_df["row_id"]
        .to_numpy()
    )

    if (
        USE_CACHE
        and cache_path.exists()
        and not FORCE_RECOMPUTE
    ):
        cached = np.load(
            cache_path,
            allow_pickle=False,
        )

        if np.array_equal(
            cached["row_ids"],
            expected_row_ids,
        ):
            return {
                "row_ids": cached["row_ids"],
                "cls": cached["cls"],
                "mean_patch": cached["mean_patch"],
                "cls_mean_concat": cached["cls_mean_concat"],
                "elapsed_sec": float(cached["elapsed_sec"]),
                "grains_per_sec": float(cached["grains_per_sec"]),
                "peak_gpu_mb": float(cached["peak_gpu_mb"]),
                "batch_size": int(cached["batch_size"]),
                "from_cache": True,
            }

        print(
            "Ignoring stale cache:",
            cache_path.name,
        )

    batch_size = int(initial_batch_size)

    while batch_size >= 1:
        try:
            result = _extract_once(
                model,
                model_key,
                normalization_spec,
                perturbation_spec,
                batch_size,
            )

            result["from_cache"] = False

            np.savez_compressed(
                cache_path,
                row_ids=result["row_ids"],
                cls=result["cls"],
                mean_patch=result["mean_patch"],
                cls_mean_concat=result["cls_mean_concat"],
                elapsed_sec=np.asarray(
                    result["elapsed_sec"],
                    dtype=np.float64,
                ),
                grains_per_sec=np.asarray(
                    result["grains_per_sec"],
                    dtype=np.float64,
                ),
                peak_gpu_mb=np.asarray(
                    result["peak_gpu_mb"],
                    dtype=np.float64,
                ),
                batch_size=np.asarray(
                    result["batch_size"],
                    dtype=np.int64,
                ),
            )

            return result

        except RuntimeError as error:
            message = str(error).lower()

            if "out of memory" not in message:
                raise

            print(
                f"CUDA OOM at batch_size={batch_size}. "
                "Retrying with half."
            )

            if torch.cuda.is_available():
                torch.cuda.empty_cache()

            gc.collect()
            batch_size //= 2

    raise RuntimeError(
        "Inference failed even with batch_size=1."
    )

13. Class-structure metrics¶

In [15]:
def l2_normalize_rows(
    embeddings: np.ndarray,
    eps: float = 1e-12,
) -> np.ndarray:
    norms = np.linalg.norm(
        embeddings,
        axis=1,
        keepdims=True,
    )

    return embeddings / np.maximum(
        norms,
        eps,
    )


def stratified_metric_indices(
    meta_df: pd.DataFrame,
    max_samples: int,
):
    if len(meta_df) <= max_samples:
        return np.arange(len(meta_df))

    classes = sorted(
        meta_df["class_id"].unique()
    )

    per_class = max(
        1,
        max_samples // len(classes),
    )

    selected = []

    for class_id in classes:
        indices = meta_df.index[
            meta_df["class_id"] == class_id
        ].to_numpy()

        rng = np.random.default_rng(
            SEED + int(class_id)
        )

        n = min(
            per_class,
            len(indices),
        )

        selected.extend(
            rng.choice(
                indices,
                size=n,
                replace=False,
            ).tolist()
        )

    selected = np.asarray(
        selected,
        dtype=int,
    )

    return np.sort(selected)


def class_centroids(
    normalized_embeddings: np.ndarray,
    labels: np.ndarray,
):
    centroids = {}

    for class_id in np.unique(labels):
        centroid = normalized_embeddings[
            labels == class_id
        ].mean(axis=0)

        centroid /= max(
            np.linalg.norm(centroid),
            1e-12,
        )

        centroids[int(class_id)] = centroid

    return centroids


def centroid_similarity_summary(
    normalized_embeddings: np.ndarray,
    labels: np.ndarray,
):
    centroids = class_centroids(
        normalized_embeddings,
        labels,
    )

    ids = sorted(
        centroids.keys()
    )

    rows = []

    for index, class_a in enumerate(ids):
        for class_b in ids[index + 1:]:
            similarity = float(
                np.dot(
                    centroids[class_a],
                    centroids[class_b],
                )
            )

            rows.append({
                "class_a": CLASS_NAMES.get(
                    class_a,
                    str(class_a),
                ),
                "class_b": CLASS_NAMES.get(
                    class_b,
                    str(class_b),
                ),
                "cosine_similarity": similarity,
            })

    pair_df = pd.DataFrame(rows)

    if pair_df.empty:
        return np.nan, np.nan, np.nan, pair_df

    mean_similarity = float(
        pair_df["cosine_similarity"].mean()
    )

    max_similarity = float(
        pair_df["cosine_similarity"].max()
    )

    bad_healthy_similarity = np.nan

    for _, row in pair_df.iterrows():
        name_a = str(row["class_a"]).lower()
        name_b = str(row["class_b"]).lower()

        has_bad = (
            "bad" in name_a
            or "bad" in name_b
        )

        has_healthy = (
            "healthy" in name_a
            or "healthy" in name_b
        )

        if has_bad and has_healthy:
            bad_healthy_similarity = float(
                row["cosine_similarity"]
            )
            break

    return (
        mean_similarity,
        max_similarity,
        bad_healthy_similarity,
        pair_df,
    )


def knn_purity_excluding_same_source(
    normalized_embeddings: np.ndarray,
    labels: np.ndarray,
    source_images: np.ndarray,
    k: int = 5,
):
    similarity = (
        normalized_embeddings
        @ normalized_embeddings.T
    )

    same_source = (
        source_images[:, None]
        == source_images[None, :]
    )

    similarity[same_source] = -np.inf

    valid_rows = np.isfinite(
        similarity
    ).any(axis=1)

    if not valid_rows.any():
        return np.nan, np.nan

    valid_similarity = similarity[
        valid_rows
    ]

    valid_labels = labels[
        valid_rows
    ]

    top1_index = np.argmax(
        valid_similarity,
        axis=1,
    )

    top1_accuracy = float(
        np.mean(
            labels[top1_index]
            == valid_labels
        )
    )

    k_effective = min(
        k,
        max(1, similarity.shape[1] - 1),
    )

    topk_indices = np.argpartition(
        valid_similarity,
        -k_effective,
        axis=1,
    )[:, -k_effective:]

    topk_labels = labels[
        topk_indices
    ]

    topk_purity = float(
        np.mean(
            np.mean(
                topk_labels
                == valid_labels[:, None],
                axis=1,
            )
        )
    )

    return (
        top1_accuracy,
        topk_purity,
    )


def separation_metrics(
    embeddings: np.ndarray,
    meta_df: pd.DataFrame,
):
    metric_indices = stratified_metric_indices(
        meta_df,
        MAX_METRIC_SAMPLES,
    )

    X = embeddings[
        metric_indices
    ].astype(np.float32)

    metadata = (
        meta_df.iloc[metric_indices]
        .reset_index(drop=True)
    )

    labels = metadata[
        "class_id"
    ].to_numpy()

    source_images = metadata[
        "image_path"
    ].to_numpy()

    Xn = l2_normalize_rows(X)

    if len(np.unique(labels)) >= 2:
        silhouette = float(
            silhouette_score(
                Xn,
                labels,
                metric="cosine",
            )
        )
    else:
        silhouette = np.nan

    knn1, knn5 = (
        knn_purity_excluding_same_source(
            Xn,
            labels,
            source_images,
            k=5,
        )
    )

    (
        mean_centroid_similarity,
        max_centroid_similarity,
        bad_healthy_similarity,
        pair_df,
    ) = centroid_similarity_summary(
        Xn,
        labels,
    )

    pca2 = PCA(
        n_components=2,
        random_state=SEED,
    )

    pca2.fit(Xn)

    pca2_variance = float(
        pca2.explained_variance_ratio_.sum()
    )

    majority_chance = float(
        pd.Series(labels)
        .value_counts(normalize=True)
        .max()
    )

    metrics = {
        "silhouette_cosine": silhouette,
        "knn1_excl_same_image": knn1,
        "knn5_purity_excl_same_image": knn5,
        "mean_centroid_cosine": mean_centroid_similarity,
        "max_centroid_cosine": max_centroid_similarity,
        "bad_healthy_centroid_cosine": bad_healthy_similarity,
        "pca2_explained_variance": pca2_variance,
        "majority_chance": majority_chance,
    }

    return metrics, pair_df

14. Feature redundancy metrics¶

In [16]:
def components_for_variance(
    cumulative_variance: np.ndarray,
    threshold: float,
) -> int:
    return int(
        np.searchsorted(
            cumulative_variance,
            threshold,
            side="left",
        )
        + 1
    )


def feature_redundancy_metrics(
    embeddings: np.ndarray,
):
    X = embeddings.astype(np.float32)

    if len(X) > MAX_METRIC_SAMPLES:
        rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)

        indices = rng.choice(
            len(X),
            size=MAX_METRIC_SAMPLES,
            replace=False,
        )

        X = X[indices]

    centered = (
        X
        - X.mean(
            axis=0,
            keepdims=True,
        )
    )

    variances = centered.var(axis=0)

    near_zero_count = int(
        np.sum(
            variances < 1e-10
        )
    )

    pca = PCA(
        n_components=min(
            centered.shape[0],
            centered.shape[1],
        ),
        svd_solver="full",
        random_state=SEED,
    )

    pca.fit(centered)

    explained_ratio = (
        pca.explained_variance_ratio_
    )

    cumulative = np.cumsum(
        explained_ratio
    )

    components_90 = components_for_variance(
        cumulative,
        0.90,
    )

    components_95 = components_for_variance(
        cumulative,
        0.95,
    )

    components_99 = components_for_variance(
        cumulative,
        0.99,
    )

    eigenvalues = np.maximum(
        pca.explained_variance_,
        0.0,
    )

    eigenvalue_sum = eigenvalues.sum()

    if eigenvalue_sum > 0:
        probabilities = (
            eigenvalues
            / eigenvalue_sum
        )

        probabilities = probabilities[
            probabilities > 0
        ]

        effective_rank = float(
            np.exp(
                -np.sum(
                    probabilities
                    * np.log(probabilities)
                )
            )
        )

        participation_ratio = float(
            (eigenvalue_sum ** 2)
            / max(
                np.sum(eigenvalues ** 2),
                1e-12,
            )
        )
    else:
        effective_rank = np.nan
        participation_ratio = np.nan

    valid_dimensions = (
        variances >= 1e-10
    )

    if valid_dimensions.sum() >= 2:
        correlation = np.corrcoef(
            centered[:, valid_dimensions],
            rowvar=False,
        )

        absolute_correlation = np.abs(
            correlation
        )

        upper = absolute_correlation[
            np.triu_indices_from(
                absolute_correlation,
                k=1,
            )
        ]

        mean_abs_corr = float(
            np.nanmean(upper)
        )

        fraction_corr_090 = float(
            np.nanmean(
                upper >= 0.90
            )
        )

        fraction_corr_095 = float(
            np.nanmean(
                upper >= 0.95
            )
        )
    else:
        mean_abs_corr = np.nan
        fraction_corr_090 = np.nan
        fraction_corr_095 = np.nan

    metrics = {
        "embedding_dim": int(
            X.shape[1]
        ),
        "near_zero_variance_dims": near_zero_count,
        "pca_components_90": components_90,
        "pca_components_95": components_95,
        "pca_components_99": components_99,
        "effective_rank": effective_rank,
        "participation_ratio": participation_ratio,
        "mean_abs_feature_corr": mean_abs_corr,
        "fraction_abs_corr_ge_090": fraction_corr_090,
        "fraction_abs_corr_ge_095": fraction_corr_095,
    }

    return metrics, explained_ratio

def plot_embedding_pca(
    embeddings: np.ndarray,
    meta_df: pd.DataFrame,
    title: str,
):
    indices = stratified_metric_indices(
        meta_df,
        MAX_METRIC_SAMPLES,
    )

    X = l2_normalize_rows(
        embeddings[indices]
        .astype(np.float32)
    )

    metadata = (
        meta_df.iloc[indices]
        .reset_index(drop=True)
    )

    pca = PCA(
        n_components=2,
        random_state=SEED,
    )

    X2 = pca.fit_transform(X)

    plt.figure(figsize=(9, 7))

    for class_name in sorted(
        metadata["class_name"].unique()
    ):
        mask = (
            metadata["class_name"]
            .to_numpy()
            == class_name
        )

        plt.scatter(
            X2[mask, 0],
            X2[mask, 1],
            s=12,
            alpha=0.55,
            label=class_name,
        )

    plt.xlabel("PC1")
    plt.ylabel("PC2")

    plt.title(
        f"{title}\n"
        f"PC1+PC2 variance = "
        f"{pca.explained_variance_ratio_.sum():.3f}"
    )

    plt.legend()
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

20. PCA cumulative variance¶

In [23]:
def plot_cumulative_pca(
    embeddings: np.ndarray,
    title: str,
):
    _, explained_ratio = (
        feature_redundancy_metrics(
            embeddings
        )
    )

    cumulative = np.cumsum(
        explained_ratio
    )

    plt.figure(figsize=(9, 5))

    plt.plot(
        np.arange(
            1,
            len(cumulative) + 1,
        ),
        cumulative,
    )

    plt.xlabel("Number of PCA components")
    plt.ylabel("Cumulative explained variance")
    plt.title(title)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


plot_cumulative_pca(
    normalization_embeddings[
        "original"
    ][BEST_EMBED_MODE],

)

21. Stage B — Robustness helpers¶

In [24]:
def same_instance_cosine(
    reference: np.ndarray,
    current: np.ndarray,
):
    reference_n = l2_normalize_rows(
        reference.astype(np.float32)
    )

    current_n = l2_normalize_rows(
        current.astype(np.float32)
    )

    similarities = np.sum(
        reference_n * current_n,
        axis=1,
    )

    return {
        "embedding_stability_mean": float(
            np.mean(similarities)
        ),
        "embedding_stability_median": float(
            np.median(similarities)
        ),
        "embedding_stability_p05": float(
            np.quantile(
                similarities,
                0.05,
            )
        ),
        "embedding_stability_p01": float(
            np.quantile(
                similarities,
                0.01,
            )
        ),
    }


def mean_class_centroid_drift(
    reference: np.ndarray,
    current: np.ndarray,
    labels: np.ndarray,
):
    reference_n = l2_normalize_rows(
        reference.astype(np.float32)
    )

    current_n = l2_normalize_rows(
        current.astype(np.float32)
    )

    reference_centroids = class_centroids(
        reference_n,
        labels,
    )

    current_centroids = class_centroids(
        current_n,
        labels,
    )

    drifts = []

    for class_id in sorted(
        reference_centroids.keys()
    ):
        similarity = float(
            np.dot(
                reference_centroids[class_id],
                current_centroids[class_id],
            )
        )

        drifts.append(
            1.0 - similarity
        )

    return float(
        np.mean(drifts)
    )

In [25]:
robustness_rows = []
robustness_embeddings = {}

labels_full = meta_eval_df[
    "class_id"
].to_numpy()

for normalization_spec in ROBUSTNESS_NORMALIZATIONS:
    normalization_name = (
        normalization_spec["name"]
    )

    reference = normalization_embeddings[
        normalization_name
    ][BEST_EMBED_MODE]

    for perturbation_spec in ROBUSTNESS_SPECS:
        perturbation_name = (
            perturbation_spec["name"]
        )

        if perturbation_name == "clean":
            result = normalization_embeddings[
                normalization_name
            ]
        else:
            result = extract_embeddings(
                model=vit_s_model,
                model_key="vit_s14",
                normalization_spec=normalization_spec,
                perturbation_spec=perturbation_spec,
                initial_batch_size=MODEL_CONFIGS[
                    "vit_s14"
                ]["initial_batch_size"],
            )

        current = result[
            BEST_EMBED_MODE
        ]

        robustness_embeddings[
            (
                normalization_name,
                perturbation_name,
            )
        ] = result

        stability = same_instance_cosine(
            reference,
            current,
        )

        separation, _ = separation_metrics(
            current,
            meta_eval_df,
        )

        centroid_drift = (
            mean_class_centroid_drift(
                reference,
                current,
                labels_full,
            )
        )

        robustness_rows.append({
            "model": "vit_s14",
            "normalization": normalization_name,
            "embedding_mode": BEST_EMBED_MODE,
            "perturbation": perturbation_name,
            **stability,
            **separation,
            "mean_class_centroid_drift": centroid_drift,
            "elapsed_sec": result["elapsed_sec"],
            "grains_per_sec": result["grains_per_sec"],
            "peak_gpu_mb": result["peak_gpu_mb"],
        })

robustness_df = pd.DataFrame(
    robustness_rows
)

robustness_path = (
    RESULTS_DIR
    / "robustness_vit_s.csv"
)

robustness_df.to_csv(
    robustness_path,
    index=False,
)

display(
    robustness_df.sort_values(
        [
            "normalization",
            "embedding_stability_mean",
        ],
        ascending=[True, True],
    )
)

print("Saved:", robustness_path)

if BEST_NORMALIZATION != "original":
    original_robustness = (
        robustness_df[
            robustness_df["normalization"]
            == "original"

    normalized_robustness = (
        robustness_df[
            robustness_df["normalization"]
            == BEST_NORMALIZATION
        ]
        .set_index("perturbation")
    )

    common_conditions = (
        original_robustness.index
        .intersection(
            normalized_robustness.index
        )
    )

    robustness_delta_df = pd.DataFrame({
        "perturbation": common_conditions,
        "original_stability": (
            original_robustness.loc[
                common_conditions,
                "embedding_stability_mean",
            ].to_numpy()
        ),
        "normalized_stability": (
            normalized_robustness.loc[
                common_conditions,
                "embedding_stability_mean",
            ].to_numpy()
        ),
        "original_silhouette": (
            original_robustness.loc[
                common_conditions,
                "silhouette_cosine",
            ].to_numpy()
        ),
        "normalized_silhouette": (
            normalized_robustness.loc[
                common_conditions,
                "silhouette_cosine",
            ].to_numpy()
        ),
    })

    robustness_delta_df[
        "delta_stability"
    ] = (
        robustness_delta_df[
            "normalized_stability"
        ]
        - robustness_delta_df[
            "original_stability"
        ]
    )

    robustness_delta_df[
        "delta_silhouette"
    ] = (
        robustness_delta_df[
            "normalized_silhouette"
        ]
        - robustness_delta_df[
            "original_silhouette"
        ]
    )

    display(
        robustness_delta_df.sort_values(

            ascending=False,
        )
    )

    robustness_delta_df.to_csv(

31. Class-wise robustness¶

In [34]:
def classwise_embedding_stability(
    reference: np.ndarray,
    current: np.ndarray,
    meta_df: pd.DataFrame,
):
    reference_n = l2_normalize_rows(
        reference.astype(np.float32)
    )

    current_n = l2_normalize_rows(
        current.astype(np.float32)
    )

    similarities = np.sum(
        reference_n * current_n,
        axis=1,
    )

    temp = meta_df[
        [
            "class_id",
            "class_name",
        ]
    ].copy()

    temp["same_instance_cosine"] = (
        similarities
    )

    return (
        temp.groupby(
            [
                "class_id",
                "class_name",
            ]
        )["same_instance_cosine"]
        .agg(
            [
                "mean",
                "median",
                "std",
                "count",
            ]
        )
        .reset_index()
    )


classwise_rows = []

for normalization_spec in ROBUSTNESS_NORMALIZATIONS:
    normalization_name = normalization_spec[
        "name"
    ]

    reference = normalization_embeddings[
        normalization_name
    ][BEST_EMBED_MODE]

    for perturbation_spec in ROBUSTNESS_SPECS:
        perturbation_name = perturbation_spec[
            "name"
        ]

        result = robustness_embeddings[
            (
                normalization_name,
                perturbation_name,
            )
        ]

        current = result[
            BEST_EMBED_MODE
        ]

        temp = classwise_embedding_stability(
            reference,
            current,
            meta_eval_df,
        )

        temp["normalization"] = (
            normalization_name
        )

        temp["perturbation"] = (
            perturbation_name
        )

        classwise_rows.append(
            temp
        )

classwise_robustness_df = pd.concat(
    classwise_rows,
    ignore_index=True,
)

34. How to interpret the results¶

Normalization¶

A normalization method is useful only if it improves class structure without damaging information that matters for grain quality.

Focus on:

  • higher silhouette_cosine,
  • higher knn1_excl_same_image,
  • higher knn5_purity_excl_same_image,
  • lower mean_centroid_cosine.

Redundancy¶

The raw embedding dimension alone does not tell us how much unique information exists.

Useful indicators:

  • pca_components_90/95/99,
  • effective_rank,
  • mean_abs_feature_corr,
  • fraction of very highly correlated dimensions.

Robustness¶

A stable representation should keep the same grain reasonably close to itself after realistic acquisition changes.

Focus on:

  • embedding_stability_mean,
  • embedding_stability_p05,
  • class separability under perturbation,
  • mean_class_centroid_drift.

ViT-S vs ViT-B¶

Do not select ViT-B only because it is larger.

It should provide a meaningful gain in:

  • class structure,
  • robustness,
  • or useful embedding rank,

that justifies:

  • more parameters,
  • more GPU memory,
  • lower throughput.

Fine-tuning¶

Fine-tuning remains outside this notebook.

It becomes justified only if:

  1. pretrained DINOv2 already contains useful signal,
  2. the remaining separation problem appears learnable,
  3. preprocessing/model-size experiments are not sufficient by themselves.
